Hi Erin —

Following up on our partner kickoff: we’re preparing the Private Offer for Acme Retail and want to lock two things quickly so we don’t slip the publishing window. Can you confirm the Marketplace team’s preference on the items below? I’ve attached the current offering draft and a short AMI checklist.

1) SKU mapping: Acme’s procurement has a preferred SKU structure (annual-subscription + three add-on SKUs). Do we register three SKUs and map them to a single Private Offer, or does AWS prefer separate offers? Also, are there naming constraints we should follow for co-sell visibility?

2) AMI vs container image: Our build produces both an AMI and a container image (ECR). For the Private Offer we plan to use an AMI image for quick onboarding. Does AWS require the AMI to be published in the partner account or can we share an AMI via snapshot with Acme’s account? Any registry/partition constraints we should be aware of?

3) Product page microcopy: attached is the current hero one-liner and three bullets. Marissa/Ben — can you review the bullets below and flag anything that will affect entitlements or compliance language? Legal will need to weigh in on the pricing footnote.

Attached: rdw_aws_offering_draft_v1.pdf, ami_build_instructions.txt

Thanks,

Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer: SKU mapping, AMI sync & product page microcopy

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline: 

1) SKU mapping: Marketplace prefers registering each billable unit as a distinct SKU. For Private Offers, you attach those SKUs to the Private Offer contract. That said, for co-sell reporting we recommend a primary SKU (the base subscription) with add-on SKUs linked as optional entitlements — this improves visibility in the Partner Central reports. Avoid special characters; use lowercase and hyphens.

2) AMI vs container image: For AMIs we typically require either (a) an AMI published in your AWS Partner account with proper launch-permission settings, or (b) an exported AMI snapshot that we copy into the customer account. Sharing an ECR image is possible but adds an extra permission step for the customer. If you plan to maintain the AMI, publish it in the partner account and set the launch permissions to the customer account ID.

3) Product page: I can loop in Marketplace PM for copy approval, but the bullets should emphasize deployment speed and cost predictability.

Contact: Diego Ramirez (diego.ramirez@amazon.com) on Marketplace enablement — he can take the AMI checklist and confirm ingestion steps.

Proposed times: Tue 1/26 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 1/27 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?

-Erin
AWS Partner Solutions
